lessonTitle: 27. Monotonicity and the derivative; critical points
lessonTitleEnglish: Monotonicity and the derivative; critical points
unit: Algebra · Chapter 4. Continuity and the derivative
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 11 mathematics textbooks (general stream)

stages.headline: Where f'(x) > 0 the function increases, where f'(x) < 0 it decreases.
stages.headlineEnglish: Where f'(x) > 0 the function increases, where f'(x) < 0 it decreases.

stages.headline: Critical points are interior points where f'(x) = 0 or the derivative does not exist.
stages.headlineEnglish: Critical points are interior points where f'(x) = 0 or the derivative does not exist.

stages.headline: For x³ − 3x: f' > 0 when |x| > 1 and f' < 0 when |x| < 1, so f increases on (−∞; −1] and [1; +∞) and decreases on [−1; 1].
stages.headlineEnglish: For x³ − 3x: f' > 0 when |x| > 1 and f' < 0 when |x| < 1, so f increases on (−∞; −1] and [1; +∞) and decreases on [−1; 1].

stages.headline: f'(x) > 0 on (a; b). What can be said about f?
